Let's be honest: Your teenage daughter, little sister, niece, or cousin is definitely the impossible-to-shop-for person when it comes to gift shopping. Their taste is impossible to nail down, and they're notoriously difficult to impress. Are Stanley tumblers still cool? Will she wear a bag charm, or is that already so last year?

Guessing is honestly a trap, and pretty much guarantees you’ll temporarily end up their least favorite person in the family. You don't want that! And neither do we, which is precisely why I've scoured the internet (and by that, I mean TikTok) to find the best gifts for the teen girl in your life—ones she'll actually love in a real and totally not fake way. I'm talking everything from cutie little makeup sets to tech gifts and beyond. There's something for every personality, hobby, and niche trend you probably didn't even know existed... until now.

A teenage girl and her photos go hand-in-hand, so you can probably assume how hyped she'll be when she sees this mini photo printer. This purse-sized gadget that requires zero ink connects to her phone via Bluetooth and will let her print photos whenever and wherever she wants.

Go ahead and splurge on a daily essential like body lotion, and she’ll ooh and ahh over it. The scents are incredible—and if she’s into layering, they’ll work well with her perfumes too.

In a recent development, A purse-friendly mirror is a must for quick touch-ups on the go. They’ll be obsessed with this cool New York-themed one!

Girls are badass gamers, too! Treat her to a fresh wireless headset so she can keep dominating the leaderboards. (She can also use these for school, if that sweetens the deal.).

Sources indicate that she’s definitely seen the Laneige lip mask in her feed and will be pleasantly surprised that you know how cool this little tub of lip moisturizer is. Nods of approval, coming right up.

They will be obsessed with these cozy slippers that are perfect for at-home study sessions and movie nights in with their besties.

Sources indicate that if she doesn't already have this Gen Z-loved sweatshirt from Lululemon, hit "add to cart" ASAP. And if she does, treat her to a latest color!

Sources indicate that this itty bitty digital camera bag charm and keychain actually functions as a camera. You can even personalize the pics with custom Kodak frames, vintage filters, and date stamps.

According to recent reports, this advent calendar is so teen girl-coded. It’s packed with beauty faves, like Vacation’s Super Spritz Travel Face Mist, Eilish by Billie Eilish Eau De Parfum Mini Fragrance, Sol de Janeiro body mist, and so much more.

If Stanley is still her tumbler of choice, we love this accessory for letting her go hands-free while still having her water bottle by her side. It wraps around the Stanley and has pockets, hooks, and a strap that lets her wear it as a crossbody.

Industry observers note that having nice luggage is a small milestone on the road to adulthood, so get her a sturdy piece she can call her own. Not to rush things, but this will come in handy when she goes away to college, too.

According to recent reports, looking for a stocking stuffer the teen in your life will actually use? This cutie Coca-Cola x Lip Smacker Lip Balm Set will be a hit.

One thing about most teenage girls? If it’s small and pink, they’re instantly intrigued. This mini perfume set from LoveShackFancy checks both boxes—and smells absolutely divine. With dreamy notes of floral and vanilla, they're the kind of scents they'll be spritzing on every day.

Beaded bags are having a major moment right now, adding instant personality to any outfit. I betcha this hotline design will promptly become her favorite!

When I was a teenage girl, yoga pants from PINK were the coolest thing you could wear. And now? This nostalgic favorite from the Victoria’s Secret brand is making a major comeback with today’s teens. Trust me, you’ll score serious cool points if you surprise her with a pair.

Teen girls and lip products go hand in hand—truly two peas in a pod. Treat them to this ultra-moisturizing set featuring the viral favorites from Summer Fridays.

Look at you thinking ahead, you! Great question. To keep things short and sweet: It’s almost too late, but you can still beat the clock with a few methods. USPS recommends shipping by December 17 for its Ground Advantage and First-Class Mail services, December 18 for Priority Mail, and December 19 for Priority Mail Express. UPS and FedEx can get a package there in time for Christmas as long as you ship by December 23 at the very, very latest (and shell out some extra cash for overnight shipping). And then there’s always Amazon Prime: If you’re a member, you might be able to score two-day or even same-day shipping, depending on the item. But don’t wait!

Why The Rings of Power Will Never Be the Same After the Season 3 Finale

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the creators and showrunners of The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power embarked on season 3, they knew the endgame from the start: The forging of the One Ring. After two seasons in the Second Age of Middle-earth, which saw almost all the other Rings of Power forged—three for Elves, seven for Dwarves, and nine for Men—it was time for Sauron to forge the one to rule them all.

“We wanted a tighter, tauter, more profound season,” notes co-showrunner Patrick McKay, in an interview with Esquire. “We wanted to start with a bang and never let up. We wanted to deepen our characters psychologically, and challenge them in latest ways. You’re seeing the end of one part of the story, and the beginning of another.”.

It has been revealed that “We had to have Sauron forge the One Ring,” adds J.D. Payne, who also created and serves as co-showrunner with McKay. “To do that, all the storylines in some way are connected to Sauron’s attempts at world domination. That was the one that so much of our attention and focus went into getting right, and it took all of our departments working together at the top of their games to create.”.

On Wednesday, just in time for Thanksgiving, Prime Video gave Tolkien fans a feast with the final two episodes of The Rings of Power season 3: episode 7, “Orodruin,” and episode 8, “The Doom of Men.”.

In the penultimate episode, Sauron (Charlie Vickers) learns from the Balrog—who talks, apparently!—how to use the fires of Mount Doom to forge the One Ring. Then, with the power of the One Ring literally in his hands, Sauron mobilizes his army for battle against Pharazôn (Trystan Gravelle), the king of Númenor. But instead of a major, violent bloodbath in the spirit of, say, Game of Thrones, Sauron simply... surrenders. Or does he? We’re talking about a master deceiver, after all.

In a spoiler-filled interview with Esquire, McKay and Payne unpack a few of our biggest questions about season 3, including how and why the Balrog speaks (with actor Simon Pegg lending his voice) to why Pharazôn is actually one of the most consequential figures in the series.

This interview has been edited for clarity.

ESQUIRE: So, wait, the Balrog can talk?

Sources indicate that PATRICK MCKAY: One of the things we're constantly trying to do is go deeper into Tolkien’s life's work. He did not just create The Lord of the Rings, he wrote all this other stuff. He envisioned an entire world. It's his legendarium. When you do the deep dive, you find there are surprising things if you only know the book and film trilogy. The Balrog Gandalf faces down in Moria is part of this level of “super being” that is equal to Gandalf and Sauron. They’re Maiar. In prior ages, Balrogs could cast spells and command troops. They’re intelligent. They can talk, you just don’t see that one talk in that circumstance.

Sources indicate that the idea of walking out onto a diving board and doing something risky, to show a different side of that being, was something that we felt compelled to do this season. It’s certainly unexpected. We’re always looking to do that. We don’t want to be familiar. We want to show you things in this world that you haven’t seen before.

Talk to me about designing a newly introduced One Ring. Granted, it’s a gold ring; there’s not much you can really deviate. But in what ways did you want to create a One Ring that belongs to The Rings of Power?

According to recent reports, MCKAY: The books are pretty specific about the way it looks. It’s a plain gold band. If you’re gonna do that, it’s going to look like the One Ring you’ve seen in other adaptations. We did make a few modifications, just for camera. We broadened it to give it more chunkiness. But it is what it says on the tin.

How is season 3 a culmination of everything that’s happened before, and how is it setting up the rest of the show?

J.D. PAYNE: It pulls together everything we’ve been doing with Sauron and Galadriel from the first two seasons. In season 1, he befriended her and deceived her in the guise of Halbrand. In season 3, you see Celebrimbor tormenting him: “You’re never gonna be able to make a ring capable of dominating all the other rings—or dominating her.” Part of Sauron’s ambition to forge the One Ring, as a character motivation, is being able to dominate the person who said “no” to him over the last few seasons. You understand how crazy that must have driven him.

MCKAY: The show’s called Rings of Power, because the creation is the throughline of this entire era of Tolkien’s mythology. At the end of season 3, you’ve now seen the creation of all of them. That’s now the world we live in. Everyone in Middle-earth is a nuclear power, so to speak. Now we’re setting up for the next part of the story, which is, “What are the consequences going to be?” One thing in season 3 we really invested in was Númenor to set Sauron up as the bowling ball crashing into those pins. That’s sort of the beginning of the end of the Second Age. It’s a tragic story. The Rings have an impact on Middle-earth that is felt for thousands of years. Now they are in this world.

According to recent reports, the finale is literally titled “The Doom of Men,” and it ends with Sauron “surrendering” to Pharazôn. Or so that’s what he wants them to think. Can you break down this moment? How is this Sauron’s big chess move?

It has been revealed that PAYNE: Everything builds up to that. You’ve seen Gandalf getting through to the Dark Wizard and take out a massive portion of Sauron’s army at the last moment. So the game changes right from underneath him, and he has to make a calculation. Is he going to put all his chips on the table and lose his army in a stalemate? Or is there another way? The great thing about Sauron is that he’s amazing at constructing scenarios that are lose-lose. If he can’t beat Pharazôn on the field of battle, he reasons maybe there’s another way. That’s why the final moment is filled with tension. It’s not simply a surrender. Our Elves, particularly Galadriel, know Sauron so well. She knows this is not a defeat for Sauron, and he’s going to find a way to make this into a play for exactly what he wants. Those who know the lore know what happens when Sauron is taken prisoner to Númenor. We wanted that feeling of dread, watching Charlie Vickers have a hint of a smile.

In a recent development, one of the most consequential characters this season has been Pharazôn. In what ways does Pharazôn represent the downfall of man?

Industry observers note that MCKAY: This is a major character in the mythology. We introduced him in season 1, he’s been sort of a politician gathering power. In season 3, he’s been king for five days, and he’s in his heyday. He’s in his golden era. But he’s driven by insecurity. There was this blacksmith we empowered, who got away, who’s now marching around saying he’s “Lord.” No, I’m the guy! There’s professional jealousy there.

It has been revealed that we talk sometimes about how he’s Stalin to Sauron’s Hitler. You’ve got two characters who are quite full of themselves, and have a high opinion of themselves, which puts them on a trajectory. Pharazôn’s goal is, “I want to take on Sauron.” That makes him a compelling character because you watch the way he greases the wheels and maneuvers to bring about that end. We give a lot of credit to our actor, Trystan Gravelle. He leaps off the screen in season 3.

Sources indicate that speaking of showdowns, one of the biggest confrontations you stage in season 3 is between Sauron and Gandalf, which Tolkien never wrote in the books. What did you hope to discover by pitting these characters together?

MCKAY: The journey of Gandalf and his involvement with Ciaran Hinds’ character, Pollando, has real deep roots in some Tolkien deep cuts where he talked about wizards who went east and that their activities probably prevented the east from joining Sauron. The story comes from that. We wanted to dramatize that through some of the most iconic characters in the legendarium coming face to face.

Industry observers note that PAYNE: Seeing the contrast between them felt like too delicious an opportunity to pass up. Sauron is seeking power at all costs, and Gandalf has been told by the Secret Fire, “To access the greatest power in the universe, you have to give up all other power.” So when Gandalf is offered the world by Sauron, he turns it down. If you demand power, it’s going to destroy you. Ultimately, having the One Ring, and forging it and trying to keep power, sets up the weaknesses of the Third Age that the heroes exploit to finally destroy Sauron.

Recent findings suggest that one of my favorite hobbies is Magic: The Gathering, which has had both Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit as crossover sets. Are there any possibilities for a Rings of Power collaboration?

In a recent development, MCKAY: [Laughs.] No. This is the first we’ve heard about it.

PAYNE: We actually wrote a draft of a Magic: The Gathering script in the before times. It was one of the last scripts we worked on before turning to Rings of Power. But it was right before the Disney-Fox merger, and it kinda got lost there. But we love that universe.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Picture this. You’re going through the grueling process that is gift shopping. You spend hours, days (but let’s be honest, not weeks because you left this for the last minute) mindlessly walking through stores, reading online gift guides, trying to find the perfect gift for every single person in your life. You check everyone off your list, one by one, until you get to the dreaded name: Dad.

In a recent development, you ask your dad what he wants and you hear the famous words “I don’t want anything,” the least helpful words in the English language. You ask your mom for help and she tells you to get him socks. You rack your brain trying to remember what he likes, what his interests are and you’re drawing blanks. Your throat is closing up, and you start breaking out in hives as the last store is about to close the night before the holiday. You reach out and, in defeat, pick up tube socks before you black out.

In a recent development, if this scene feels too familiar, then you’re going to want to read this roundup. Whether your dad is up to date on all the latest tech, whether he’s a golf enthusiast or not, we’ve rounded up the 26 best gifts for the old man who taught us everything we know.

Whether you wanna pull an uno reverse card and be the one to get him a bike for a change, the comfiest loafers he’ll ever break in, or an espresso machine that will make you even more excited for your next visit, we’ve got you covered on all the things your dad actually wants, but won’t tell you.

The biblically accurate dad shoe (complimentary). He’ll look great running his errands, walking to the coffee shop, and doing any other dad-activity you can think of while also being comfortable.

Just because he’s going to bed, doesn’t mean he shouldn’t do it in style. This 100 percent cotton set by American Classic Brooks Brothers is the perfect gift for a classy man year-round.

Sources indicate that boys love Tommy John undies. This luxe modal set is buttery soft, breathable, and the exact touch his top drawer deserves—especially if this boxer collection looks like it hasn't been upgraded since 2011. These don’t bunch, ride up, or stretch out, which he'll appreciate when he keeps them for another decade. For a pack of three, they're reasonably priced—not cheap but not over-the-top, either.

Industry observers note that if you want a stocking stuffer that’s tiny but mighty, this rechargeable keychain flashlight is it. Don’t be fooled by its size—this thing is bright, durable, and perfect for everything from late-night dog walks to finding dropped keys in the abyss of the car. It detaches magnetically and charges fast (there's an integrated USB plug in the tail, so there's no need to fuss with cords or batteries to recharge), making it the kind of gadget he’ll use and won't just throw into his junk drawer. See? Great things do come in small packages.

Instead of carrying around his deck of cards in the flimsy paper case it comes in, a leather one with his initials will keep them much more protected and looking a whole lot more elevated.

If his happy place is the golf course, get him this pouch. It clips right onto his bag and keeps all the essentials (tees, balls, markers) in one place so he can pretend he’s more organized than he actually is. The drawstring cinches tight to seal everything inside when he moves from hole to hole, and opens up if he wants to stash more stuff in need be. Choose from a bright khaki, steely gray, or classic black to fit his vibe. Whatever you go with, it'll look professional, even if his handicap… is not.

This digital meat thermometer has over 50,000 reviews on Amazon, so it's clearly a fan favorite. It reads temperatures in just three to four seconds with a 4.3-inch stainless steel probe, and the display automatically rotates 180 degrees so left-handed people can read it easily. The screen is backlit for grilling at night, and it has motion sensing technology that turns it on when you pick it up and off when you set it down to save battery. It's waterproof, has a magnetic back so it sticks to your grill, and comes in two colors!

In a recent development, we all know that guy who doesn't go anywhere without his emergency hot sauce—this Tabasco keychain set was made for him. Look how cute those mini bottles are! And the keychain cap means he can clip it right to his keys or backpack and always have a spicy snack handy. For $15, it's peak stocking-stuffer energy for foodies (or the men who pretend to be foodies).

Recent findings suggest that if he's constantly staring at screens all day, this heated eye massager is a total game-changer for tired eyes. It uses oscillating pressure and rhythmic percussion to massage around the eyes, plus it has built-in heating pads that warm to a comfortable 104-113 degrees Fahrenheit. The mask blocks out light completely, making it perfect for relaxation or better sleep. It folds into a compact design so he can take it on planes or to the office, and the adjustable headband fits all head sizes. It comes in multiple colors and is right now on sale for $53 (regularly $76). Once he tries this, he'll be using it every night.

In a recent development, if he insists on going out for a run even in freezing temps (brave), this fleece neck warmer from lululemon is a winter essential. It's made with lightweight, sweat-wicking fleece that has strategically placed perforations over the nose and mouth so he can breathe easily during his workout. The extra-long front tucks into his jacket to block cold drafts, and there's a cinchable drawcord in the back to adjust the fit.

Industry observers note that this four-in-one charging cable is honestly genius for travel. It has USB-C, Micro USB, iOS, and Apple Watch charger ports all in one braided nylon cable, so he can charge his phone, AirPods, and watch at the same time without packing multiple cords. The cable is four feet long, comes with a velcro strap to keep it organized, and has a magnetic Apple Watch charger built in. It's compatible with iPhones, most Android phones, and Apple Watch Series 1-10. Plus, it's under $10!

If he's a wine drinker who hates when his glass gets warm halfway through (or if you're tired of him complaining about it), this stemless wine chiller is genius. You freeze the cradle for at least three hours, attach it to the stand, place your stemless glass on top, and pour—the chiller keeps the wine cold for up to 90 minutes indoors or 45 minutes outside in the shade. Honestly, it's one of those products that seems almost too simple to work, but it actually does.

This tiny glow-in-the-dark ghost keychain is adorably simple and surprisingly addictive to play with. It's a squishy little ghost that glows after being exposed to light, and it comes on a keychain so he can clip it to his keys, backpack, or wherever. It's available in multiple colors, including regular and glow-in-the-dark versions. Perfect for anyone who appreciates weird little trinkets or just needs something to attach to their keys that isn't boring.

Every golfer needs a good towel, and this one from Par Bleu Golf is stylish enough to earn a permanent spot on his bag. It’s ultra-absorbent, quick-drying, and designed to keep his clubs and golf balls looking clean instead of…whatever they usually look like. Plus, it looks way more chic than your average course freebie towel, so he’ll feel just a little bit fancy out there. Choose from classic plaids, bright strips, even fun prints like fish and flowers.

Or better yet, get a towel for him. If he's always stealing your expensive exfoliant and girly body wash, put this in his stocking ASAP. This Japanese shower towel has gone viral for its buffing prowess that literally turns skin baby soft in just one use. Since it's long and flexible unlike regular loofahs, he can scrub all the hard to reach places like his back, thighs, and... wherever else. Hey, don't judge—just be happy to have your cleanser back.

According to recent reports, speaking of cleanser, if his shower routine right now involves a single mystery bottle that allegedly “does everything,” elevate his whole vibe with this Dr. Squatch soap trio. Each bar smells like a rugged man who chops wood and exclusively wears flannel—think bourbon barrels, mountain air, and fresh forest trails. They’re made without harsh chemicals, so his skin will actually thank you. Bonus: You get to enjoy the upgraded scent situation every time he walks by. AND you get to keep your skincare goodies to yourself.

Nothing says "I love you" like forcing someone to wear your face on their feet. Upload a photo of yourself, his dog, or—if you're feeling chaotic—his favorite pro athlete? It's unhinged, it's hilarious, and he'll absolutely wear them.

For the athlete (or the guy who trains like one) (or the guy who's just always complaining about random muscle pain), this compact Theragun Mini is a recovery essential. It delivers percussive massage therapy to relieve muscle soreness and tension, and it's small enough to toss in a gym bag or carry-on. It comes with three different attachments—a dampener for sensitive areas, a standard ball for full-body massage, and a thumb attachment for targeting lower back muscles and trigger points. There are three speed settings you can control via LED indicators, plus it connects to the Therabody app via Bluetooth for guided routines. It's available in six colors and is right now on sale for $180 (regularly $200).

It has been revealed that if your guy loves golf, this personalized ball stamper is genuinely such a thoughtful gift. You can customize it with his initials, name, or a monogram right on Amazon before adding it to your cart. It comes with five different ink colors (black, blue, red, green, and purple) so he can mark his balls with his own design. The stamp creates a waterproof imprint in seconds, and when the ink starts to fade, he can just refill it. At under $10, it's an affordable stocking stuffer that's actually useful.

17 Best Beard Trimmer Picks, Tested by GQ Editors in 2026

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every guy needs the best beard trimmer for his situation.
  • Industry observers note that I tested a bunch of beard trimmers to deliver you a real who’s who of men’s grooming devices.
  • Here are the best beard trimmers after we tested pretty much every last one of them.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every guy needs the best beard trimmer for his situation. Whether he grows it patchy, keeps it perma-stubbled, or is as lustrous as the A-List beards, a trimmer is mandatory in every beard kit. And not all beard trimmers are alike, which is why the best one for your facial hair style may be different from the next guy’s.

Industry observers note that I tested a bunch of beard trimmers to deliver you a real who’s who of men’s grooming devices. This list reflects a range of options—some multitaskers, some detailers; some top-shelf, some a better buy for lower budgets. Above all, though, I ask you this: Make sure that the device you choose allows your beard to reach its full potential. That doesn’t mean you need a substantial bushy beard, but rather, you should be able to achieve whichever style (or a suite of styles) you want to wear over the next few years—which is the minimum amount of time any of these devices should last. Ideally, they’ll hum on for five to 10 years, anyhow.

Here are the best beard trimmers after we tested pretty much every last one of them. (And while you’re at it, consider my rosters of other grooming tools, from razors and electric shavers, to manscapers and hair clippers.).

Recent findings suggest that black Friday is here, and the deals are hitting fast. For the biggest and swerviest markdowns, editor favorites, and elite-level shopping intel, keep it locked on our roundup of the best Black Friday deals and best Black Friday clothing deals.

No sense in burying the headline: Philips Norelco’s Multigroom 9000 Series is, hands down, the best beard trimmer you can buy. And that’s before factoring in how much more it can do than just keep your facial hair in check than other electric razors that are found in your everyday grooming kit. (It’s also recently been renamed the “All-in-One 9000” but answers to both names.) For the last 5 or 6 years, this has been my single go-to trimmer. Everything else is trying to dethrone it, and so far, no true contest has emerged. In terms of customization and power, this device checks all of the boxes.

According to recent reports, it all starts with the beating heart: "The Multigroom does not compromise on power or battery life, and it's very intuitive to use," says Fellow Barber’s Head of Education Emily Clark. The battery life truly over-delivers: your mileage may vary since Philips Norelco only claims a (still impressive) six hours of charge, but I got a ridiculous 17 hours of consecutive runtime fresh out of the box, thanks to a lithium ion battery. Speaking of the box, there’s a lot in there, all of it useful. Between the small tooth-like detail attachment and foil shaving head, the Multigroom 9000 makes it easy to style and sculpt with precision. One trimmer even adjusts by tenths of a millimeter to help you get the perfect designer stubble, if that's your aim. And that’s just its beard trimming bona fides. The Multigroom 9000 is also a solid hair trimmer (shout out to that brawny motor and battery again) and body hair trimmer as well. Covering off for three products, and doing it well, suddenly makes the $90 price tag look like a deal.

Long-term testing notes: Wouldn’t you know it… I lost the beloved little shaver on this one recently. Heartbreak. (Yeah, I can test a upcoming one, but I realize now how much of my love for it is pinned on that micro shaving attachment.) I stand by the fact that it’s the best on the market, but without that shaver, the window has opened for me to spend time with other devices, like the Braun below. Let this be a lesson: Don’t unpack your Philips Norelco all-in-one in a hotel room without carefully auditing every single piece when you pack it up again. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

According to recent reports, "This trimmer is great! It comes with so many attachments to use for your trimming needs. The battery lasts a long time, i have yet to have to charge mine and i've had it for a few months now.

Recent findings suggest that the trimmer is super quiet as well as very well made. It's all made up of metal, not plastic, and feels like it will last a long time. It's fairly lightweight and easy to handle when [using] it. It also comes with a small cleaning brush that makes cleaning it up a breeze!".

Given how much I love the Philips Norelco Multigroom 9000, it’s no surprise that the more affordable model, the Multigroom 5000, is my budget choice to keep things manscaped. It offers most of the same steel-bladed precision and customization benefits as its fancier family member, albeit in a less durable body (plastic instead of stainless steel) and half the battery life. Still, its a three-hour battery power beast that bests many beard trimmers twice the price. And the lighter plastic body is nice for travel. The Philips Norelco Multigroom 5000 is great for anyone on a budget, but it’s not “budget.".

Whereas other lower-priced beard trimmers can’t handle precise detailing, the Multigroom 5000 includes a detail trimmer and nose trimmer, not to mention hair clipper and body trimmer guards for versatility. It does lack the shaving detailer and the body shaver (as does the in-between 7000 model), which is important to note if you want that level of customization and don’t otherwise own a detail shaver that you also rely upon for bare-faced stretches of facial real estate. For this reason, I find it a little less perfect across the board compared to the 9000, but the price-to-precision ratio is hard to match. And if you want a great value above all—and a straightforward beard trimmer—meet your optimal Multigroom, the 5000.

Long-term testing notes: Recently, I used the 5000 consistently, and got quite cozy with it. Sure, it lacked the key shaving features of the 9000, but I think this is truly the best value device in the game when you only want a trimmer. Terrific muscle, terrific customization, great endurance. Five stars for this one. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

"This Phillips/Norelco trimmer works great. It is very quiet, the battery life is pretty long and it does exactly what I need it to do. It comes with a lot of attachments - haven’t used them all, but the ones I have used worked just fine. This is a good quality trimmer.".

Hatteker is a surprise of a buy—it’s that “out of left field” Amazon brand that most of us recognize by name, despite not knowing anyone who uses it. This all-in-one kit covers every kind of hair-trimming task, from lineups to sideburns to beards, eyebrows, and body hair. What's more, it's a hair-cutting machine for full beards and stubble alike with multiple plastic guards. I bought the tool with little expectations for quality and care, but was consistently surprised at how well it held its own compared to the more reputable brands.

This device won’t win any design awards and certainly hasn’t reinvented the wheel, but most consumers won’t care about that stuff; they want a good beard trimmer that meets all their grooming needs, and Hatteker’s checks all of those boxes. I do wish its detailing trimmer was a bit narrower, but that’s me minding some very fine details. It’s also not up to the same quality as, say, Philips, Andis, Braun, Wahl, etc, but it’s also not low quality either. For $40, you get your money’s worth, especially considering that LED battery display and vast range of trimming lengths and clipping attachments. It’s still a great option if you’re not looking to spend a lot, or if our other best value winner, the Philips Norelco Multigroom 5000 Series, is out of stock.

Long-term testing notes: Every time I bring this one out, I am amused by how surprisingly great it is. It goes to show that those Amazon reviews really are one of the most accurate depictions of value; I long wrote the brand off because of its non-image compared to the major names, but in terms of performance and return on spend, Hatteker really clears the bar. Granted, I’m not using most of these devices more than a few times a quarter (since by and large I stick with my own favorites or test newly introduced ones) but my Hatteker remains strong and sturdy and has endurance, some three years after I first acquired it. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

Sources indicate that "The trimmer is easy to use and the charge lasts a very long time. I have not had to recharge since the initial charge after taking it out of the box, trimming bi-weekly. It is not heavy. It’s easy to handle. The adjustment guides stay where you select. I don’t worry about them shifting during use. Beard maintenance is an easy job with this.”.

The All-in-One 7000 makes a convincing case for clearing some space in your bathroom cabinet. A body hair trimmer that comes replete with several beard-related attachments, its precision comb kept stubble neatly between 1-3mm without pulling or leaving stray hairs behind. Sure, a dedicated beard trimmer will do a more precise job, but there's plenty of substance to this device's delirious accessory count.

Industry observers note that the slightly boxy handle feels reassuringly secure when I'm cleaving away at a couple of days' growth, while a textured grip makes it well-suited to comfortably swerving across my chest, underarms, and more sensitive areas. If you dig them out from the bottom of their box, the nose and ear attachments prove useful enough to earn their place in the kit too. Philips rates this kit for up to five hours between charges – handy given how often you'll be using the thing – and the waterproof construction makes cleanup straightforward.

According to recent reports, my main gripe is one that always crops up when I test Philips, Braun, and other established grooming brands’ devices – the proprietary charging connection. You’ll need its supplied cable, even if your drawer is already overflowing with USB-C leads. Still, for someone who wants to maintain short facial hair and keep the rest of their grooming in order with one tool, the 7000 covers a lot of ground. Esat Dedezade.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

“It's comfortable and quiet with an easy-to-adjust head that's great for both beard and mustache maintenance. The precision comb is handy for controlling length too, and there's very little tugging around the neck. And if you leave it a little too long to get your beard into shape? It holds its charge surprisingly well when tucked away in a bathroom cabinet.”.

In a recent development, like the Philips Norelco Multigroom models, Braun's All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 is a jack-of-all-trades option that can do far more than tidy up your beard; the box is packed with a nose and ear trimmer, a precision head, and longer guards, too. But what separates this trimmer from the rest of the pack is the built-in dial that offers 40 trim-length settings. It’s top-notch precision in minimalist packaging. I think it’s the only real contender for the top spot on this list—perhaps that price and slightly less enduring battery are its shortcomings compared to the Philips Norelco 9000, but I do find it a superior device in terms of ease and design.

Where other devices require you to swap out different heads or attachments, or ask you to pick between bigger length gaps than you’d prefer, Braun’s Series 9 offers half-millimeter increments from 0.5 to 20 without having to futz with extra accessories. In my testing, that made the trimmer the most user-friendly device on this list—no swapping guards as you fade your beard or neckline. Plus, the Series 9 is fully waterproof for those of you shaving-in-the-shower fans looking to speedrun your morning regimen. (And I’ll admit, shaving in the shower certainly makes clean-up—of both the beard hair mess and the trimmer—faster and easier.) Bottom line, Braun’s All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 is exactly what the name promises. If it seems a little expensive, that’s because a beard trimmer that can handle all these tasks, and handle them well, isn’t cheap.

Long-term testing notes: As I said above, this one has been getting lots more mileage from me lately, and I am so pleased with that fact. I absolutely adore how easy it is to navigate between the smallest minutiae of trimming lengths without swapping guard heads, and that detail shaver has been so clutch at keeping my neckline, cheeks, and beard perimeter cleaned up. My one complaint from a recent trip was that it’s quite difficult to repack everything into the carrying case, if you bring along all attachment heads. Besides that… perfect grooming tool. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

“Before this trimmer came into my life, I made a couple of cheap purchases. The style I like it's 1mm overall with a 2mm on my chin and 2.5 on my mustache. The problem was the other trimmers could not handle it on a daily basis. I am the type of guy whose beard grows back really fast, so I'd trim my beard. Then, the next day, you could see clear growth, and when I tried to do it again, it just wouldn't trim the same. I'd end up hurting my face a little bit. Not this trimmer. This trimmer can handle my beard on a daily basis without hurting my face. It's that good and efficient. It's built for heavy performance and durability. For the first time I am able to maintain my beard on a daily basis.”.

Recent findings suggest that wahl is a pedigreed name in the professional and home grooming worlds, but that doesn’t mean it’s done innovating. Its new High Visibility trimmer has a killer app: the trimming attachment is angled so the teeth sit “above” the base, letting you get eyes on the action in the mirror as you mow through facial hair. It’s maybe not a priority if you’re just doing leisurely trims, but if you’re trying to get the perfect line at your cheek, sideburns, or neck, that little bit of offset is a godsend.

Industry observers note that suddenly I’m seeing very clearly exactly where the blade is hitting. If you’ve ever had to drop that cheek line too far down or do the back-and-forth thing with your burns, you’ll recognize what a game changer this is. The Wahl High Visibility trimmer’s laser-pointer precision is boosted by some of the best ergonomics in the game. The body’s relatively thin with an excellent rubber grip, which lets you hit difficult angles like a professional pool player. The High Visibility trimmer is latest to the market, but I’m betting it’ll become a barber favorite—and yours, too, if you’re doing daily touch-ups to keep those lines looking sharp.

Long-term testing notes: I find myself using this more often as a detail trimmer than a full-on trimmer. I think it’s a fantastic trimmer through and through, but I pull it from the bullpen as a closer; that’s where I hold it mostly in my mind—and happily! Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

Sources indicate that "Absolutely amazing product. Heavy, rock-solid construction makes the hand feel confident, has great ergonomics, and has a solid grip even when the hand is soapy. But the best part is the forever blade makes it easy to see what’s getting cut, even with guard on (I used the 2). Most precise edge for a jawbone line beard I’ve ever had. And with the guard, it combs as it cuts with the grain of the hair, keeping stray whiskers knocked down. I’ve been pinched/cut before with fatter spaced blade rakes, but I didn’t feel threatened trimming under the nose.".

Industry observers note that the MultiShape lets you build a grooming kit around the things you actually use. Start with this beard and hair trimmer, then add a nose trimmer, foil shaver, or even a toothbrush head if you want them. Everything shares one rechargeable handle, which makes much more sense than finding room for another charger every time you buy a new device. Other manufacturers – take note.

Industry observers note that this starter kit includes the lithium-ion base, beard and hair head, and two combs. The other attachments cost extra, so factor those in before deciding how much money or luggage space it’ll save. Panasonic rates the battery for 90 minutes, with a one-hour charge.

Long-term testing notes: Over several weeks, I used a broader MultiShape kit for shaving, beard maintenance, and brushing his teeth. Swapping heads was quick, and the light handle made the shared system easy to live with. The beard head coped with ordinary growth, although particularly stubborn hair exposed its limits. With daily toothbrushing and shaving three or four times a week, he charged the handle roughly every fortnight. That convenience made it a favorite for travel, while a dedicated beard trimmer remained the stronger choice for dense growth. Owen Gough.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

Industry observers note that "The upside of buying a beard trimmer that can double-up as an electric toothbrush with the right attachment is you've got one tool to rule them all. The challenge? You might need a couple of passes with the trimming head to get an even finish. Compared with the more traditional alternative, it's a bulkier device with its guard fitted.”.

Recent findings suggest that for anyone whose morning routine involves keeping a few days’ growth under control, the dedicated Beard Trimmer 7000 keeps things pleasingly straightforward. Its adjustment dial covers 40 lengths, while the textured handle gives you something secure to hold before the first coffee has kicked in.

The dial is the main reason to choose this over a kit with a bag of fixed guards. You can adjust the length without hunting for the next comb, then use the detailing attachment to tidy the edges. It’s a more focused choice than Philips’ all-in-one kits if beard maintenance is the job you actually need done. Just don’t mistake the hair collector for a return of the old vacuum trimmer – it’s another part to empty and clean.

Recent findings suggest that long-term testing notes: I found the Series 7000 easygoing around my chin and sideburns, with little cleanup needed for stray hairs. Its reassuring weight and textured grip also helps, even if the plastic finish isn't quite on par with Philips' now-retired all-metal Series 9000. Truthfully, this trimmer did struggle a little around the awkward patch beneath my nostrils with its bulky combs making it harder to get a neat finish. I also don't bother much with the removable hair collector – I'd rather clean the sink once rather than wash another attachment. As an everyday trimmer, this is still a solid pick. Rob Leedham.

“This trimmer is perfectly functional for its price, and its two-hour battery life means I'm yet to be caught short without any charge mid-shave. As much as I appreciate its efficiency, I do miss how the older metal design looked on my bathroom sink-top. This plastic iteration feels cheap (and a little flimsy) in comparison.”.

No attachments; no problem. For a beard trimmer that can only do one thing (but is damn good at doing that), Manscaped's Beard Hedger will make light work out of the bushiest, burliest beards. Its zoom wheel controller lets you dial in the comb's length between .5 and 10 millimeters for even shaves, while the waterproof construction means you can shower and shave to save time on your morning or nighttime rituals. The built-in comb is great for picking up hairs that are stuck to your face so that every strand gets whacked, because few things are more unsightly than stray long hairs poking out from an otherwise well-groomed beard. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

“I've owned maybe 5 or 6 beard trimmers over the last 15 years. Make no mistake, this is the most expensive, but hands down it's also the best (that includes competition from Braun, Philips Norelco and Wahl). The quality is the first thing you notice as soon as you unbox it - the feel of the handle and the quality of the blade, even down to the USB charging cable which doesn't have the usual cheapness you'd expect from an accessory that's something of an afterthought.”.

It has been revealed that if you’re researching beard trimmers, you’ll see the term “zero-gap” a lot. So, what’s a zero-gap trimmer? A zero-gap trimmer cuts as close to the skin as possible, effectively a 0mm cutting length. That can make them dangerous for novices, as you can easily cut your skin or ears while you trim. But for the highest possible level of precision, that’s what you want. (The Bevel Trimmer can also be adjusted so it has a slightly longer taper.).

It has been revealed that this trimmer was designed by Black men, for Black men, and damn does it look good. It’s a work of art that design lovers will appreciate. This sculptural device will look mighty impressive on your bathroom counter and feels phenomenal in your hand. It’s a true barber-quality trimmer, perfect for guys with curly or Afro-textured hair. It’s also one of the most powerful trimmers for home use, with a 6,000 RPM motor. Despite that, it beats all comers in terms of battery life, with an 8-hour charge that will last for months. A word of warning: This trimmer doesn’t come with any attachments or comb guards. That’s by design, as it’s a precision trimmer for making clean lines and shaping up longer beards. If you want to cut precise hair lengths, opt for the Bevel Trimmer Pro or purchase extra attachments like the T-Blade. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

"I’ve been cutting my own hair for years. Let me tell you these are the best trimmers I’ve ever used. Nothing on the market compares. I mean every word. The best!!!! Switch the original blade that comes with it out with the t-blade and I promise you that line up gone be crispy like bacon! Bevel with T-Blade is King!!!".

Industry observers note that one more Philips Norelco device, for good measure and good reason: This tool is adored by both our expert source and me: I love the OneBlade for its ability to switch between trimmer, shaver, T-blade, and body groomer with aplomb. I think it's one of the best-designed tools in facial hair care right now, and a dozen other brands are releasing dupes to chase the same high.

Industry observers note that “I appreciate how affordable it is and how easy it is to find at drugstores since so many clients ask me where to buy it because they love it too,” notes DeZarate. “There was one week where I needed to buy three of the OneBlade for different clients during press events, so that they were able to actually travel home with it because they loved how easy it is to use and that it's universal. It does a really nice job at creating clean lines and is great for sensitive skin.” This one is easy to torque in different directions, too, allowing its shaving function to act like a T-blade trimmer while also offering familiar cartridge-shave movement for anyone who wants an entirely clean mug or simple a neckline tidy up. Get one with the body grooming attachment, too, and you could have an all-in-one grooming device for all facial and manscaping needs; it really does it all with that one singular blade.

Long-term testing notes: Like DeZarate, I frequently reach for this guy to mind the details; it’s an easy tag-along for any trips (especially if I need some body trimming all the while) and will certainly be with me on a massive three-month trip I have to take soon; it’s a terrific head-to-toe customizer, though I don’t necessarily rely on it when I’m at home and have dedicated devices for each task. It is a terrific middle-ground pick, for the guy who wants things streamlined. Adam Hurly.

What Amazon Reviewers Are Saying.

“I have to admit, I’ve avoided this product for the past few years. For some reason I didn’t think it was something I needed. I recently started maintaining my beard on my own more and needed something with a bit more precision. Safety razors and straight razors were cutting up my face. My $200 electric razor cuts good, but is terrible at getting straight edges. So I figured I would give this a try and I must say I’m very happy with it. This is a very high quality product for the price. Not only does this razor provide the precision I needed to line up my beard, but it also shaves very very well.”.

Vacuum trimmers keep you from having dozens of errant clippings littering the sink, but this one is more than just a vacuum—it has a detailing and edgework attachment and can trim up to 18 mm with a line-drawing detail head that rivals most T-blade trimmers.

Panasonic's wet/dry beard trimmer has a convenient wheel that lets you switch between guard lengths effortlessly—a huge boon when you're trying to shape your beard.

A display screen on your beard trimmer? In this economy? If it seems too good to be true, we get it, but this easy-adjusting trimmer from Panasonic is, in fact, the real deal.

Sources indicate that for just 25 bucks, you can get this all-in-one trimmer from Philips that does a surprisingly good job when it comes to shaping and maintaining your scruff. Is it the fanciest trimmer on the list? No, but it works.

You want a beard trimmer that’s simple, effective, and doesn’t come with useless features or add-ons. Here are a few features to consider when looking for a great beard trimmer.

We look at how evenly a trimmer cuts, how comfortable it is to use, and whether its attachments make different jobs easier. Power matters, but so do the small frustrations that become obvious with regular use – awkward combs, difficult cleanup, or a handle that’s hard to hold. We also compare battery life, charging, and the range of cutting lengths against the price.

According to recent reports, adam Hurly has reviewed grooming products since 2013, and his years of testing underpin this guide. Timothy Beck Werth contributes his own hands-on findings alongside his wider coverage of grooming and consumer technology. For this update, we’ve also drawn on my reviews for British GQ, with the relevant tester and any differences between British and US kits identified in the entries. Read more about GQ and how we test and review products.

What is the best beard trimmer?

Industry observers note that there’s no denying: The Philips Norelco Multigroom 9000 is the best beard trimmer you can buy these days. If its $100 price tag is too steep, the baby-brother Multigroom 5000 is a solid fallback. It’s not shower-proof, has a shorter warranty (five years to the 9000’s eight years), has a plastic body instead of steel, and comes with a few less attachments. But at $40, it gets the basics done nearly as well as it’s pricier sibling.

Can you use a beard trimmer to cut head hair?

Beard trimmers are not meant to be used as hair clippers, since clippers require much more power to cut through thicker patches of hair. However, some beard trimmers have the muscle to multitask, and they’ll proudly hype that skill—usually by declaring the work for “beard and head” or similar language. We usually verify those claims against product reviews, too. And frankly, we’d probably just opt to buy a dedicated hair trimmer (you can find our roundup of the best hair trimmers here), especially if you’ll be using it often.

Which beard trimmer do barbers use?

Barbers choose tools to suit the job, from adjustable trimmers for controlling length, to detail trimmers for sharper edges. The Wahl Pro Series High Visibility is our professional pick for precision work, while the Philips Norelco Multigroom range offers broader versatility. For home use, start with your beard length and the kind of maintenance you do most often – a tool built for crisp outlines won’t necessarily include the guards you need to trim a longer beard evenly.

Which trimmer number is best for a beard?

Industry observers note that that's going to depend on what beard style you're going with. In order to play around with trimmer numbers, we like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440 for its easy-to-use adjustment wheel.

How do you use a beard trimmer?

According to recent reports, first, wash and dry your beard so you're starting off with a clean canvas. Then, decide how short or long you want to keep that bad boy. Trim against the grain of your growth, and know that the direction of growth may vary even in similar locations on the face. It's OK to make a couple of passes to ensure you get each hair because a patchy beard is a bad beard. Finally, clean up the neckline with some sharp lines so it's neat and tidy, framing the perfection that is your beautiful facial hair.

How do I maintain and clean a beard trimmer?

Switch it off and disconnect the charger before cleaning, then remove trapped hair from the blades and combs after each use. Follow the instructions for your particular model – a washable cutting head doesn’t mean the whole handle can go under the tap. The Remington Vacuum trimmer, for example, has removable washable parts, but its body should stay out of water.

Let washed components dry before putting them away. Oil the blades if the manufacturer tells you to, but don’t assume every trimmer needs it. Philips’ current Multigroom blades are designed to work without oiling. Replace a damaged or persistently blunt cutting unit with the correct part for your model.

How do I choose the right trimmer if I have sensitive skin or ingrown hairs?

Avoid “zero-gap” trimmers, which is a trimmer that cuts as close to the skin as possible, effectively a 0mm cutting length—those can mess your skin if you're prone to irritation or ingrowns. Otherwise, since you're trimming, you usually won't have to worry about irritating your skin because the blades shouldn't ever actually make contact with your face.

What’s the best way to travel with a beard trimmer—any TSA or voltage concerns?

According to recent reports, one of the massive concerns for frequent travelers—at least in the USA—is whether they're going to be able to get their beard trimmer through security and not having it buzz during transport. If this is a priority for you, look for a model with a travel lock like the Braun All-in-One Trimmer Series 9 9440, which prevents the trimmer from turning on in transit.

How do I clean a waterproof vs. non-waterproof trimmer?

In a recent development, waterproof trimmers are a breeze: Just hit ‘em with the (usually included) cleaning brush, then wash them off in the sink before drying and applying some oil. Non-waterproof trimmers just skip the rinse, so you’ll have to take extra care with the brush. You can also use spray cleaners specifically designed for grooming electricals depending on your trimmer's care instructions.

What should I do if my trimmer starts pulling hair or losing power?

First, make sure you've thoroughly cleaned the trimmer. Next, make sure it's fully charged and/or has new batteries. If it's still pulling hair, it's probably time to swap the blades (plenty of companies sell refills on their site, and make sure to check the warranty to see if you qualify for a fresh set). If it's losing power, it might be time to swap the internal battery (check your warranty!) or get a new trimmer altogether. Luckily, we haven't had that matter with any of the trimmers listed above.

Emily Clark is Head of Education at Fellow Barber and a Senior Barber at Fellow’s SoHo NYC barbershop.

Melissa DeZarate is a celebrity groomer whose clients include Matt Damon, Kenan Thompson, Matt Bomer, and Taika Waititi.

#157960. Forget Plymouth Rock This Thanksgiving. American History Is Better Reflected by a Different Stone.

Forget Plymouth Rock This Thanksgiving. American History Is Better Reflected by a Different Stone.

📅 26 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (855 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Let me send out a little Thanksgiving advice to potential tourists planning to visit us in the Commonwealth (God save it!) in the future.
  • First of all, Plymouth Rock is a boulder in a hole in the ground.
  • Even Alexis de Tocqueville, America’s greatest tourist and, therefore, its primordial sucker, fell for the Rock’s charisma.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Let me send out a little Thanksgiving advice to potential tourists planning to visit us in the Commonwealth (God save it!) in the future. If some local tells you to go to see Plymouth Rock, tell them you have tickets for a four-day Duck Tour of the Freedom Trail. I promise you: Seeing Paul Revere’s house four times is infinitely more interesting than seeing Plymouth Rock once.

First of all, Plymouth Rock is a boulder in a hole in the ground. Oh, there’s a classical templish thing above it, but it’s still a boulder in a hole in the ground. Second, there’s almost no historical evidence that any pilgrim feet ever trod upon the rock in question. None of the contemporaneous accounts mention it. It was a nonagenarian named Thomas Faunce who, in 1741, 121 years after the Mayflower arrived, decided that this was the rock on which all the Bradfords and their shipmates disembarked. It moved around Plymouth a lot in the early years. In 1774, it cracked in two, which some folks took as an ill omen for the burgeoning Revolution. (Pieces of it are in the Smithsonian) The year 1620 was carved into the boulder’s surface in 1880. In 1920, it found its permanent home. In 1990, writing in The New Yorker, John McPhee wrote of the rock:.

Even Alexis de Tocqueville, America’s greatest tourist and, therefore, its primordial sucker, fell for the Rock’s charisma.

Sources indicate that damn, Alexis. Have some Madeira and chillez out, mon ami.

If you want to see a genuinely interesting boulder, drive 42 minutes west to the town of Berkley, where you will find Dighton Rock State Park. In another templish building, there is Dighton Rock. It is a six-sided, five-foot-high slab of sandstone. It is also adorned with ancient petroglyphic carvings of uncertain origin. There are depictions of animals and an assortment of lines and whorls and mysterious designs. In 1680, John Danforth got a look at the Dighton Rock and not even his recently bestowed Harvard degree could explain them. He made drawings of the carvings he could see. (At the time Danforth saw it, the rock was partially submerged in the Taunton River.) It also drew the interest of local celebrities like Cotton Mather and poet James Russell Lowell.

Industry observers note that danforth’s opinion was that the carvings were made by the local Native tribes, and he thought it depicted an ancient battle of some sort. (If there’s anything like a consensus among people who have studied the carvings, it’s Danforth’s.) However logical that might seem, it didn’t tamp down speculation as the years went by. Down through the centuries, the carvings have been attributed to Phoenicians, Carthaginians, Vikings, Portuguese adventurers, Chinese explorers, and Japanese mariners. And, of course, inevitably … aliens.

However, it was a professor of psychology from Brown University who had the right of it, I think. Edmund Delabarre was a well-respected psychological researcher in the first half of the 20th century. He also grew fascinated with the study of rock carvings in and around Narragansett Bay. Ultimately, his researches brought him to the shores of the Taunton River and to the Dighton Rock.

Sources indicate that ultimately, Delabarre dismissed all the other claims of origin and concluded that the carvings on the Dighton Rock were probably made by a crew sailing under the command of one Miguel Corte-Real, a Portuguese explorer who charted about 600 miles of coastline in and around the Canadian Maritimes. In 1502, Corte-Real set sail for the western Atlantic, seeking to discover what had become of his brother, Gaspar, who had not returned from a voyage to Newfoundland. Miguel vanished, too.

Sources indicate that delabarre’s contention was that Miguel had made it to Upcoming England, and he argued that the inscription was a form of abbreviated Latin that proclaimed Corte-Real to be “king of the Indians.” In his 2017 book The Place of Stone, Douglas Hunter pretty much demolished all of the outre interpretations of the carvings, arguing that the carvings were of Native origin, and that the other interpretations were elements in the erasure of Native history and the legacy of bloody colonization, of which, ironically, the settlement at Plymouth was Ground Zero. The people who didn’t step onshore on a rock in Plymouth launched one of the first campaigns of the greater American genocide. As Hunter wrote:.

Sources indicate that so there’s American history on the Thanksgiving of 2026, ground up between two stones, one a legend with a counterfeit past, and another a mystery with a stolen past. The latter is by far the more compelling. Its history encompasses all of the history, good and bad, of this appropriated continent. Edmund Delabarre was wrong about Miguel Corte-Real and the Portuguese, but he might have been more right than he knew when he wrote that Dighton Rock was a kind of test. In the ambiguity of its carvings at the time of Delabarre’s work, a person saw in them what he wanted to see. Not all of it was pretty, or ennobling, or triumphal. But it's all ours.

This Jewelry Designer Bride Created Her Own Vintage-Inspired Dress for Her Polish Countryside Wedding

💡 Key Takeaways
  • When the Polish jewelry designer Natalia Kopiszka was planning her August 2026 wedding to actor Aleksander “Olek” Kaleta, she found herself at a bridal fashion crossroads, stuck between two stylistic pillars of her own brand: vintage and modern.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When the Polish jewelry designer Natalia Kopiszka was planning her August 2026 wedding to actor Aleksander “Olek” Kaleta, she found herself at a bridal fashion crossroads, stuck between two stylistic pillars of her own brand: vintage and modern.

First, the Warsaw-based designer of Kopi traveled to Paris to shop for a vintage wedding dress, but returned home empty-handed. “I didn’t find anything that I liked, so I thought: I will design my own wedding dress,” Natalia says.

For the body of her ceremony dress, she ordered fabric—silk taffeta—from Etsy. “I was on a mission to find the absolute dream silk fabric,” she states. “I started by checking out local fabric shops and silk wholesalers, but I just couldn't find the right silk taffeta with that delicate, subtle sheen anywhere.” She searched online and stumbled upon a listing from a Fresh York-based seller, which she ordered on the spot. Luckily, “it turned out to be even more breathtaking in person than in the photos,” she says.

Then, on a weekend trip to Amsterdam with a friend, she wandered into a vintage store where she found antique lace, which she used for the bodice detailing. “The lace is truly unique because it dates back to the early 20th century, and I only had a tiny piece of it—which happened to be just enough to trim the bodice,” Natalia says. “It was such a special way to check off the ‘something old’ tradition.” She sketched the dress, then shared her designs with a dressmaker who sewed it, making her vintage-modern dream a reality.

According to recent reports, natalia and Olek first met in February 2021 at a house party in Warsaw. “For me, it was love at first sight,” Natalia recalls. “A friend of mine who lived in the apartment below me threw a get-together, and her roommate happened to be friends with Olek. As soon as he walked in, we instantly locked eyes. I’m pretty sure he was the one who came over and started the conversation first,” she adds. “It also turned out that Olek lived directly across the street from my apartment, so we used to wave at each other from our windows. Ever since that night, we started seeing each other almost every single day.”.

Sources indicate that after a year, they moved in together in Warsaw. In 2024, Olek proposed to Natalia during a trip to Italy, in the coastal town of Polignano a Mare. “It was a warm, romantic evening with a huge moon, and surprisingly, I didn't see it coming at all,” Natalia says. “It turned out to be such a sweet, funny moment because neither of us could stop laughing.”.

In a recent development, on August 8, 2026, the couple held their wedding at Pałac Pstrokonie, a historic 19th-century palace in a small village outside of Warsaw. They worked with the wedding planner Kasia Fastyn, who brought Natalia’s vision—a romantic, whimsical wonderland of sorts—to life, pairing them with the event studio MyBigDay, who designed the florals and draped their dancing tent in pink fabric.

Recent findings suggest that as a jewelry and accessories designer, Natalia zeroed in on all the details of her wedding looks from the beginning. She knew she didn’t want a traditional floral bouquet, for example, so she opted for a small silk bag in the shape of a bouquet from the Fresh York-based designer Camille Albertine, after finding her work on Instagram. Albertine custom-made Natalia’s bouquet purse in the same fabric as her dress. “Everyone was so surprised that I didn’t have a typical bouquet,” Natalia indicates. “It’s versatile enough that I can wear it with everyday outfits. It’s going to stay with me for a long time, and I’ll even be able to pass it down through generations.”.

It has been revealed that for her reception look, the bride changed into a dress by the Polish designer Magda Butrym, pairing it with an unexpected accessory: a crochet veil cap that her sister made. “It was a really simple dress, also silk, but I put something really crazy on my head,” Natalia says.

Natalia incorporated her own jewelry into the crochet cap-like veil, which was bedazzled with charms and pendants. “They are specially made charms with little lobster clasps so you can clip them onto the crochet work however you like. They’re gold-plated and feature Swarovski crystals,” Natalia claims. (Charms are a signature of Natalia’s brand, she explains, so it was only fitting to work them into her bridal looks.) Her love of historical pieces, particularly from the Victorian era, inspired the final design, which included blue stones for her “something blue.” A look inspired by it is now for sale as part of Kopi’s “I Do” bridal line.

The bride also made Olek a pocket square with the same vintage lace as her dress, so they were matching (and so he had “something old” as well). They completed their looks with wedding bands that Natalia designed. “Mine has a retro feel, crafted in gold and set with 12 small diamonds,” she notes of the rings. “Olek went for a classic look—a simple, wide gold band with my nickname engraved on the inside.” Reflecting on the wedding months later, Natalia says: “Everything was perfect.”.

Denmark’s Queen Mary is looking posh and joyful on day two of her historic state visit to Colombia—a trip which makes her the first Danish queen to travel to the country.

Today, the monarch was given a tour of the Gold Museum in Bogotá, and later walked through the city’s main square, Plaza de Bolívar, with Mayor Carlos Fernando Galán.

The official visit runs through November 26, and the queen’s agenda includes learning about the country’s post-earthquake reconstruction efforts (three months after a 7.4-magnitude earthquake struck Colombia) and ongoing sustainability projects.

To arrive in the country, Mary went sharp in a black Forte Forte single-breasted blazer with a frilly sky-blue Stenströms Darya blouse, which she paired with black trousers, Malone Souliers Marion 70 pumps, and black Gucci glasses, plus some gold jewelry.

In a recent development, then, for this afternoon’s engagements, she slipped into a sophisticated business look, the highlight of which was a black-and-white tweed pencil skirt from Dolce & Gabbana and a black collared top from Red Valentino. To round out the ensemble, she reached for sheer black tights, plus matching stilettos and a leather handbag.

The royal performed another quick change for her evening engagement: a reception in the Biodiversario greenhouse at Bogotá’s Botanical Garden. The look was a breezy wine midi dress with a fun dotted print by Saloni. In semi-sheer fabric, it featured a high neck, long sleeves, a cinched waist, and a long skirt that reached her ankles. Black-and-white heels added the perfect contrast to the colorful maxi.

Industry observers note that he’ll be ready for the wilderness at a moment’s notice, even if the wilderness hasn’t called yet. Until it does, pick any of these and you’re covered, no camping required.

Industry observers note that made from ballistic nylon, which is a fancy way of saying it can take a beating. The bridle leather handles keep it handsome enough for a meeting, all while being tough enough to survive getting tossed in the back of a truck he doesn’t own.

Recent findings suggest that the official footwear of the guy whose favorite trail runs from the couch to the fridge. Cozy enough to lounge in all weekend and good-looking enough that he’ll “accidentally” wear them to get the mail.

For the guy who insists vinyl just sounds warmer, despite not having the tech to prove it. The built-in preamp means it plugs straight into speakers, so there’s no excuse not to finally play that record he bought for the cover.

In a recent development, yes, it's a Jeff Goldblum fragrance, and yes, it's actually great. Brain Dead's collab opens with sandalwood, tobacco leaf, and leather, so it smells like a campfire at a very nice lodge. He'll get compliments, and he'll credit Jeff.

Japanese selvedge with all the rugged good looks and none of the miserable, stiff-as-cardboard break-in period. Ideal for a man of action, or at least a man who looks great standing next to a campfire.

The kind of sweater that looks like it was passed down from a grandfather who really knew how to chop wood. The two-tone brown and black knit goes with everything from denim to cords, and it'll only get better with every passing winter.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that malin Akerman may stir up romantic trouble as Margo Banks, the notorious ringleader of The Hunting Wives, but off screen, her love life is much less chaotic. The actress has been happily married to fellow actor Jack Donnelly since 2018, and over the years, the two have even found ways to merge their professional and personal lives.

In a recent development, akerman and Donnelly have collaborated on several projects, including four movies (and an NSFW sex scene, but more on that below). In a 2023 interview with People, the actress opened up about their relationship, crediting her husband with helping her become a better communicator.

“He’s allowed me to be vulnerable and lean into him a bit, and it’s been beautiful to be able to communicate with someone who’s your partner,” she stated of their marriage.

Ahead, everything you need to know about Jack Donnelly, his career, and his marriage with Akerman.

Donnelly was born in Bournemouth, England, on October 28, 1985, and later attended the Central School of Speech and Drama in London. He made his acting debut in 2011 on the Nickelodeon series House of Anubis. Two years later, he landed a breakout lead role in the BBC’s series Atlantis, as Jason—which remains one of his best-known roles to date.

According to recent reports, in addition to acting, Donnelly has branched out behind the camera as a television writer and director. He wrote, directed, and starred in the short comedy series The Players, which debuted in 2023.

In a recent development, the couple’s love story began with a family connection. Donnelly first met Akerman through her younger sister, whose boyfriend was friends with him at drama school. During a 2018 appearance on Live With Kelly and Ryan, the actress explained that she had actually known Donnelly for several years before their relationship turned romantic.

Industry observers note that “I had known him for the past four years but didn’t see him,” she recalled. “Then all of a sudden he came back from England like a year-and-a-half ago, and I went, ‘Wow, have you always been this cute?’”.

Akerman confirmed the couple’s engagement via Instagram in October 2017. Sharing a selfie with Donnelly and flashing her upcoming engagement ring, she captioned the post, “This sweet and loving man has stepped into our lives and stole both our hearts,” she wrote, referring to her and her son. “I think we’re gonna keep him around for a while,” she continued with a wink.

According to recent reports, akerman and Donnelly tied the knot a little over a year later, on December 1, 2018, in a beach ceremony held in Tulum, Mexico. “It was all about being authentic...not adhering to somebody else’s standard of what a wedding should be,” Akerman told Brides.

According to recent reports, “We wanted something beautiful and lush,” she continued, sharing more about their wedding venue. “When we visited Papaya Playa Project [in Tulum], we fell in love with the boho vibes and beach setting.”.

In 2023, Akerman shared latest photos from the beachside wedding on Instagram to celebrate their five-year anniversary.

In a recent development, when discussing her engagement on Live With Kelly and Ryan in 2018, Akerman also shared how excited her son, Sebastian, was about the news. The actress shares Sebastian with her ex-husband, musician Roberto Zincone, and recalled his excited reaction when she told him that she and Donnelly were getting married. “He jumped up on the couch and went, ‘Yay, we’re getting married!’” she said.

Industry observers note that in another 2018 interview with Us Weekly, Akerman gushed about the close bond Donnelly had already formed with her then-five-year-old son. “They’re inseparable,” she stated. “It makes my heart warm. I’m very glad to be bringing Jack into our lives for good.”.

Over the years, the three have also made several red-carpet appearances together, offering a glimpse into their life as a family.

In a recent development, akerman and Donnelly have shared the screen in four films so far: Friendsgiving, A Week in Paradise, Slayers, and Us or Them. Their first movie together was the 2020 comedy Friendsgiving, in which they played a couple—and even had to film a steamy sex scene. During a 2020 appearance on The Talk, Akerman opened up about filming the “crazy S&M scene.”.

According to recent reports, “[It was] just like being in our home,” she joked when asked what it was like filming the sex scene. She added that she was glad to have her husband as her costar. “Any chance I get to have him do a scene like that, who better than to do it with than your husband?” she noted. “It’s a really, kind of, intimate, crazy scene, and thank God we know each other well enough instead of just meeting somebody on the first day and [doing] this crazy S&M scene. It was lovely to have him there.”.

It was a far cry, fashion-wise, from the past few weeks in Catherine’s diary. A visit to India for the Earthshot Prize ceremony with the Prince of Wales saw her inadvertently twinning with Bridgerton’s Simone Ashley in Mumbai, and wearing a hand-embroidered anarkali by Latest Delhi designer Mahima Mahajan, paired with jewels from Queen Elizabeth II’s collection.

Kate wearing the same jacket three years ago in South Wales.

According to recent reports, the late Queen, though, would certainly have approved of the princess’s practical winter uniform—Barbour’s waxed jackets were central to her own outdoor wardrobe when staying at blustery Balmoral or Sandringham. (Granted, Her Majesty’s version was not from an Alexa Chung capsule, like Kate’s.) According to fashion folklore, when Barbour offered to replace the monarch’s well-worn Beaufort style, she chose to keep the original for another 25 years. Like her husband’s grandmother before her, given the opportunity, Kate always looks happy to swap occasionwear for clothes better suited to navigating muddy fields—like waterproofs and walking boots. Her check-lined jacket has been in her wardrobe since at least 2023, when she wore it on a visit to South Wales with her husband.

At the Hugo Burge Foundation in Greenlaw, Scotland.

Recent findings suggest that little wonder the princess looks so comfortable in her outdoor gear. Kate Middleton is famously passionate about nature, and the sporty royal completed the grueling Three Peaks Challenge over the summer after recovering following treatment for cancer. Over the weekend, the palace released an emotional trailer for Heal, a deeply personal documentary in which Catherine reflects on her cancer diagnosis and recovery.
